x: Ian Badiali won his 440 yds. heat in 51.9 secs., and was placed 5th in the final, which was in 49 seconds by Arthur Wint who was running for the Hospitals.

The 440 yds. saw Arthur Wint "strolling" round the track to record 50.4 secs and "Jock" Cameron ran well to gain 2nd place for us. In the final event, the 1 mile medley relay, our team of Bob Taylor, Bartlett, Holtum and Bob Wolton finished 3rd behind the Poly. and Achilles in 3 mins. 35 secs.

In the Middlesex Championships Bob Taylor was second in the 880 yards for the third year in succession. He equalled Arthur Wint's County record in his heat, but a slow first lap in the final prevented a fast time, and he was beaten by R.
Three Belgravians lined up with over 120 others to be sent on their way by 1948 Olympic 400m Champion, Arthur Wint, now High Commissioner for Jamaica.

He won no less than 7 Berkshire A.A.A. titles at 100, 220 and 440 yards in the early 1950's and was a member of the Polytechnic 4 x 110 and 4 x 440 relay teams which includeded Macdonald Bailey, Arthur Wint and Brian Shenton, and which won A.A.A. titles.
Arthur Wint brought off the difficult 440/880 double prior to his Olympic success. Jim Peters emerged with a win in the 6 miles having not yet moved up to the marathon distance.

The 880yds, probably the finest race of the Championships, seemed to be a struggle between Arthur Wint and the visiting New Zealand Champion Doug Harris until a few yards from the tape when both were overwhelmed by John Parlett's late surge.

The second day's programme produced a record equalling run in the domestic 220 by McDonald Bailey in 21.2, a good 440 yds win by Olympic Champion Arthur Wint in 48.1 and the first of many wins by John Disley in the 2 mile steeplechase.
The 400 metres seemed to be a straight contest between the usual strong USA trio and Jamaica with George Rhoden, Herb McKenley and Arthur Wint.
Bob Taylor equalled the Middlesex record held by the great Arthur Wint in the 880 yards, and Ivan Mayers beat Ron Holtum in the sprints while Jack Brown won the Kent one mile.
